name: Candidate first-integral drift
mathematical_definition: Evaluate explicitly supplied invariant callbacks I(x) in physical coordinates x=D y; report I(x0) and max over stored samples of |I(xk)-I(x0)|.
operational_scope: trajectory or point; separate certified domain claim allowed

coordinate_convention.time: tau=t/Ts with positive Ts; stored time arguments remain physical t
coordinate_convention.norm: L2 for vectors/operator norm; Frobenius only where stated

null_and_failure_states.policy: null means unavailable, never zero-imputed; projection requires matching version, scope, evidence and a finite numeric non-boolean field
null_and_failure_states.construction_errors: Invalid state/scale or mutated binding can raise ValueError before an AxisResult is produced.
null_and_failure_states.high_dimension: Dense Jacobian dependencies are unsupported above max_dense_dimension (default 64); only z08 uses directional fallback.

evidence_permissions.numerical: Measurements are point/trajectory observations with proposition_truth unknown, not universal proofs.
evidence_permissions.declaration: Applicable supplied model claims remain declared with unknown truth; mathematical prose is not independently verified.
evidence_permissions.analytic: Only implemented structural constructions may assert their narrowly stated result: z01 dimension; z18 authoritative finite polynomial no-pole claim.
evidence_permissions.certified: Supported independently verified bound claim kind first_integral. Concrete certificate must bind authoritative expression AST, parameters, state box, requested time interval, and scales; the independent verifier recomputes it. Numeric output remains separate.

mathematical_boundary: No complete invariant discovery; small sampled drift does not prove Lie derivative zero.
implementation_limitations: A reference may cover a subinterval; inspect requested/evaluated intervals and full_original_window before claiming full-horizon coverage.
Default reference, RHS and Jacobian samples are numerical approximations, not interval bounds.
